label: Common
description: Weight-update parameterizations shared across editing, continual learning, and unlearning.

full_finetuning.label: Full fine-tuning
full_finetuning.title: Update all trainable parameters
full_finetuning.summary: Full fine-tuning optimizes **every trainable model parameter** using the selected task objective. The objective may target editing, continual learning, or unlearning, with preservation terms where appropriate.
full_finetuning.formula_explanation: This is a gradient-descent update for a generic task loss L. All trainable parameters can change. Optimizers such as Adam use a different update rule based on the same gradients.

terms.name: Updated parameters
terms.description: All trainable weights after the step.

terms.name: Current parameters
terms.description: All trainable weights before the step.

terms.name: Learning rate
terms.description: Controls the size of a gradient-descent step.

terms.name: Gradient
terms.description: The derivative of the task loss with respect to model parameters.

terms.name: Task objective
terms.description: The objective selected for editing, continual learning, or unlearning.

steps: Choose the task objective and any preservation or retention terms.
Evaluate the objective on a training batch.
Apply the optimizer update and evaluate target behavior and retained capabilities.

constrained_finetuning.label: Constrained fine-tuning
constrained_finetuning.title: Fine-tune within an update budget
constrained_finetuning.summary: Optimize a **cumulative perturbation Δ** across all trainable parameters while keeping its **norm strictly below ε**. This parameterization applies to editing, continual learning, and unlearning with the corresponding task objective.
constrained_finetuning.formula_explanation: Optimize the selected task objective at θ + Δ. Keep θ fixed throughout optimization and constrain the cumulative change Δ, not only each individual optimizer step. Choose a norm and a positive budget ε.

terms.name: Updated parameters
terms.description: The model parameters after adding the learned perturbation.

terms.name: Reference parameters
terms.description: The fixed model parameters at the start of adaptation.

terms.name: Cumulative update
terms.description: The learned difference between the adapted model and the fixed reference model.

terms.name: Update norm
terms.description: The size of the cumulative update under the chosen norm.

terms.name: Update budget
terms.description: A positive upper bound. The update norm must remain strictly below this value.

steps: Keep a **fixed copy of the reference parameters θ** and initialize Δ to zero.
Evaluate the selected task objective using the adapted parameters θ + Δ.
Compute gradients with respect to Δ and propose an optimizer step.
If the proposed norm reaches or exceeds ε, rescale Δ to a radius strictly smaller than ε under the chosen norm.
Repeat while enforcing the **cumulative norm budget**, then use θ′ = θ + Δ.

lora.label: LoRA
lora.title: Low-Rank Adaptation
lora.summary: LoRA **freezes the base weight** and learns a **scaled low-rank update BA**. Use the selected editing, continual-learning, or unlearning objective, including any preservation or retention term.
lora.formula_explanation: For \(W_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times k}\), \(B \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\) and \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{r\times k}\). **Only \(A\) and \(B\) are trained.** The update has **rank at most \(r\)**; \(\alpha/r\) scales it.

terms.name: Frozen base weight
terms.description: The pretrained weight matrix W₀ ∈ ℝ^(d×k), held fixed during adaptation.

terms.name: Low-rank output factor
terms.description: A trainable d×r matrix, initialized to zero.

terms.name: Low-rank input factor
terms.description: A trainable r×k matrix, randomly initialized. The rank r is much smaller than d and k.

terms.name: Adapter scale
terms.description: α is a scaling hyperparameter and r is the adapter rank.

steps: Select the weight matrices to adapt and **freeze the base model weights**.
Choose rank r and scaling α; initialize A randomly and B to zero.
**Optimize A and B** using the selected task objective and any preservation or retention term.
Evaluate target behavior and retained capabilities; merge the scaled BA update into W₀ if desired.

dora.label: DoRA
dora.title: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
dora.summary: DoRA **separates weight magnitude from direction**. It learns a **magnitude vector m** and uses **low-rank factors to adapt direction**. Use the selected editing, continual-learning, or unlearning objective, including any preservation or retention term.
dora.formula_explanation: The denominator contains **one L2 norm per column**, not a single matrix norm. Normalize each column of W₀ + BA, then scale it by its learned magnitude in m. Multiplication and division broadcast column-wise. Adapter scaling is absorbed into BA here.

terms.name: Frozen base weight
terms.description: The pretrained weight matrix W₀ ∈ ℝ^(d×k), held fixed during adaptation.

terms.name: Low-rank output factor
terms.description: A trainable d×r matrix, initialized to zero.

terms.name: Low-rank input factor
terms.description: A trainable r×k matrix, randomly initialized. The rank r is much smaller than d and k.

terms.name: Magnitude
terms.description: A trainable value for each column, initialized to the L2 norm of the corresponding column of W₀.

terms.name: Normalized direction
terms.description: Each column of W₀ + BA is divided by its own L2 norm. A and B train the direction while W₀ stays frozen.

steps: Freeze W₀ and initialize each magnitude in m from the corresponding column norm of W₀.
Initialize A randomly and B to zero, so the initial effective weight equals W₀.
Form the column-normalized direction from W₀ + BA and multiply by m.
**Optimize m, A and B** using the selected task objective and any preservation or retention term; the paper detaches the normalization denominator during backpropagation.
Evaluate the adapted model and, if desired, materialize the effective weight for inference.
